h1: The 7 Best Bookshelves with Drawers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Bookshelves with Drawers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 bookshelves with drawers scored on drawer type, footprint and capacity, from slide-out cabinets to fabric-bin units.
summary: The FINETONES 71 inch double-wide bookshelf is the best bookshelf with drawers: four wrap-around drawers and eight open shelves in a rigid engineered-wood frame. The DICTAC suits narrow walls with three slide-out drawers on 24 inches of wall, and the Furologee is the cheap corner option. The EXPERLAM adds solid pine.
intro: Most bookshelves give you open shelves and call it storage. The trouble starts the day you own more small stuff than books: chargers, remotes, mail, craft supplies. Open shelves turn that pile into visible clutter, and that is the entire reason a drawer exists. A bookshelf with drawers is really a hybrid of a bookcase and a chest.

We reviewed seven shelving units that pair open display space with closed storage, from rail-mounted drawers to lift-out fabric bins. Each was ranked on how much it stores, how wide it stands, how the drawer works and what the frame is made of, using spec sheets and what owners report. A drawer that sags or jams loses its point fast, so the build counted as much as the drawer count.

products.name: FINETONES 71" Double Wide Bookshelf + 4 Drawers
products.verdict: Four drawers plus eight open shelves in one wide, rigid frame. It swallows a whole room's clutter.
products.description:
The FINETONES is 39.4 by 11.8 by 70.8 inches, with four wrap-around drawers, eight open shelves, thickened engineered-wood panels, metal handles and an anti-reverse belt. Twelve storage zones in one unit, with about 38 lb per shelf, let it replace both a bookcase and a dresser.

It ranks first because it stores the most and the panels resist sagging. The DICTAC is narrower but has three drawers, and the cheaper units have one.

Buy it to swallow a whole room's clutter. The caveats are the roughly 40 inches of wall it needs, heavy weight once built and engineered wood rather than solid. Skip it if your wall or alcove is under 40 inches.
pros: Twelve storage zones in one unit
Four real drawers with metal handles
products.idealFor: People who want one wall unit to replace a bookcase and a dresser.
products.skipIf: Your wall or alcove is under 40 inches wide.

products.name: DICTAC 73.23" Tall Storage Bookcase + 3 Slide-Out Drawers
products.verdict: Three smooth-glide drawers on a 73-inch frame that only needs 24 inches of wall.
products.description:
The DICTAC is 73.23 inches tall, 23.62 wide and 14.2 deep, with three smooth-glide slide-out drawers, three open tiers, a top storage zone, a waterproof scratch-resistant surface and an anti-tip kit. A tall frame on a 24 inch footprint suits narrow walls and pantries.

It ranks second because it has fewer drawers than the FINETONES and only three open tiers. It is tall, so it must be anchored.

Buy it for narrow walls, pantries and bathrooms that need closed storage. Skip it if you want lots of open shelving for large books. Fasten the kit to a stud. Smooth-glide drawers hold clutter out of sight, and the waterproof surface suits a damp room. A top zone offers a place for baskets, but keep heavy items low to reduce wobble.
products.idealFor: Narrow walls, pantries and bathrooms that need closed storage.
products.skipIf: You want lots of open shelving for large books.

products.name: Furologee 5-Tier Bookshelf + 1 Removable Fabric Drawer
products.verdict: The cheapest way in, with a lift-out drawer and a 15-inch footprint.
products.description:
The Furologee 5-tier is 15.4 by 10.6 by 55.5 inches, P2 MDF and metal, with five open shelves rated 30 lb each (150 lb total), one removable fabric drawer, four leveling feet and an anti-tip kit. A lift-out bin is easy to clean.

It ranks third because it has only one drawer and a fabric bin that is not rigid. It is the cheapest in the ranking.

Buy it for dorms, kids' rooms and tight corners on a budget. Skip it if you need several hard-sided drawers. Leveling feet help on uneven floors. Lift the drawer out to wash it, and avoid heavy items, since the fabric sags. The metal frame adds stiffness over an all-MDF build, but 150 lb total is a modest rating.
pros: Lift-out bin is easy to clean
products.idealFor: Dorms, kids' rooms and tight corners on a budget.

products.name: EXPERLAM 8-Cube Solid Pine Bookshelf + 4 Fabric Storage Bins
products.verdict: Real pine instead of MDF, with four collapsible bins and a flexible cube layout.
products.description:
The EXPERLAM is a 47 by 11.8 by 24 inch eight-cube unit in solid pine, with four collapsible 11 inch fabric bins, two removable back panels and a layout that works vertically, horizontally or as a room partition. Solid pine resists sagging better than MDF.

It ranks fourth because the bins are not true drawers and the unit is only 24 inches tall flat. Cube openings limit tall books.

Buy it for kids' rooms and studios that need a flexible solid-wood cube unit. Skip it if you want rail-mounted drawers or a tall tower. The finish is odor-free and kid-safe, and the bins collapse flat when you need to store them. As a divider, it needs the back panels fitted so items do not fall through.
products.idealFor: Kids' rooms and studios needing a flexible, solid-wood cube unit.
products.skipIf: You want rail-mounted drawers or a tall tower.

products.name: SUNMORY 6-Tier Tree Bookshelf + 2 Storage Cabinets
products.verdict: A tree-shaped shelf with two joinable cabinets and a two-year warranty.
products.description:
The SUNMORY is a 6-tier tree-shaped shelf, 47.4 by 14.6 by 7.9 inches, in MDF with two open joinable cabinets, a two-year warranty with lifetime support and an anti-tip kit. The tree shape is decorative.

It ranks fifth because it is only 7.9 inches deep and the cabinets are open, not closed. It is a lightweight build.

Buy it for small bedrooms and entryways wanting a decorative shelf. Skip it if you need to store large books or closed drawers. The warranty is the best here, at two years with lifetime support, and the cabinets can be joined for a wider look. Its shallow depth limits it to paperbacks and decor, so do not expect it to hold a full library.
products.idealFor: Small bedrooms and entryways wanting a decorative shelf.
products.skipIf: You need to store large books or closed drawers.

products.name: Furologee 5-Tier Ladder Shelf + 1 Removable Fabric Drawer
products.verdict: Ladder shape widens at the base for a 215 lb total rating.
products.description:
The ladder-style Furologee is 16.53 by 11.42 by 55.51 inches, with a black metal frame, P2 MDF shelves, backboards on every shelf, one removable fabric drawer, four adjustable feet and a 215 lb total capacity. The ladder shape widens toward the base.

It ranks sixth because it still has only one drawer and a soft-sided bin. Its footprint is slightly larger than the 5-tier.

Buy it for the ladder look with a higher load rating. Skip it if you want more than one drawer. Backboards stop small items falling behind, and the 215 lb total rating gives more room than the five-tier version. The industrial style suits a loft or a kids' study, and the feet level it on uneven floors.
products.idealFor: Buyers who like the ladder look and want more load rating.
products.skipIf: You want more than one drawer.

products.name: Evermagin 6-Tier Tree Bookshelf + Light + 1 Storage Drawer
products.verdict: The only one here with a built-in lamp, but it is a light-duty shelf.
products.description:
The Evermagin is a 6-tier tree shelf, 15 by 7.9 by 57.87 inches, in P2 MDF, with a built-in adjustable lamp with three color temperatures, one storage drawer at the base, space for 30 to 50 paperbacks and an anti-tip kit. A shelf with a light suits a reading nook.

It ranks last because it is shallow, light-duty and has only one small drawer. It is the only one with a lamp.

Buy it for reading nooks that need a shelf and light in one. Skip it if you store hardcovers or heavy items. Keep to paperbacks and leave heavy volumes on sturdier shelves. The lamp lets you read without a separate light, but the shallow frame limits what the base drawer holds. Check the cord reach before you place it.
products.idealFor: Reading nooks that need a shelf and light in one.
products.skipIf: You store hardcovers or heavy items.

methodology.title: Drawer type and count
methodology.description: We separated rail-mounted drawers from fabric bins and open cabinets, because they solve different clutter problems and fail in different ways.

methodology.title: Footprint versus storage
methodology.description: Width and depth were weighed against total storage zones so a bigger unit had to earn its wall space.

methodology.title: Frame material
methodology.description: Solid pine, thickened engineered wood and thin MDF were ranked by how rigid each should stay across years of load.

methodology.title: Load rating
methodology.description: Stated per-shelf and total capacities were compared against what a typical book collection weighs.

methodology.title: Safety features
methodology.description: Anti-tip hardware and drawer designs were checked, since tall units and small children are a common pairing.

whatMatters.detail: Rail drawers slide on tracks and close out of sight, which hides clutter well but can fail at the track. Fabric bins lift out and collapse, so there is nothing to jam, but they sag and show their contents. Check the listing photos for the drawer front and note whether it says slide-out or removable. The DICTAC and FINETONES use real drawers, and the Furologee and EXPERLAM use fabric.

A shelf under about 8 inches deep only suits paperbacks, while hardcovers and binders need 11 inches or more. The depth is often buried in the spec list. Measure your largest book, then compare it with the listed depth before you assume it will fit. The SUNMORY and Evermagin are 7.9 inches deep.

A total rating can hide a weak individual shelf. A full shelf of hardcovers can top 30 lb, so look for the per-shelf figure and not only the whole-unit number. If only a total is listed, divide it by the shelf count to get a rough ceiling. The FINETONES lists about 38 lb and the Furologee 30 lb per shelf.

Solid pine feels sturdiest, thick engineered wood is the middle ground, and thin MDF bows first. The listing usually says P2 MDF, engineered wood or solid wood. Choose the heavier material if the shelf will hold books. The EXPERLAM is solid pine, the FINETONES uses thickened engineered wood, and most of the others are MDF.

Tall narrow furniture can fall forward when drawers are pulled open. A wall anchor kit prevents that. Look for an anti-tip kit in the box contents, and plan to screw it into a stud, which matters most with children in the home. The DICTAC, Furologee, SUNMORY and Evermagin list one.

faq.q: Are drawers or open shelves better on a bookshelf?
faq.a: Open shelves display and hold books best, while drawers hide small items from view. If you own both, a unit like the FINETONES that combines four drawers and eight shelves is the better compromise.

faq.q: Can a bookshelf with drawers go in a bathroom or kitchen?
faq.a: Only if the finish is moisture resistant, and even then keep it away from direct splashes. The DICTAC lists a waterproof, scratch-resistant surface, which is why it suits pantry and bathroom use better than standard MDF.

faq.q: Do I need to anchor a tall bookshelf to the wall?
faq.a: Yes, for anything above about 50 inches, because tall units tip when a drawer is open. Opening drawers shifts weight forward. Use the included anti-tip kit and fasten it into a stud, especially for the 73-inch DICTAC.

faq.q: Is solid pine worth it over MDF?
faq.a: For heavy books and years of use, yes, since solid wood holds screws better. Solid pine like the EXPERLAM resists sagging better. For light decor and a few paperbacks, MDF is fine and costs less.

faq.q: How do I stop shelves from sagging under books?
faq.a: Keep heavy volumes on the lowest shelves, stay under the per-shelf rating and avoid spans over about 30 inches without support. Spread weight evenly across shelves. Thicker panels, as on the FINETONES, sag less.

faq.q: Can fabric drawers hold heavy items?
faq.a: They suit clothes, toys and lightweight clutter, which makes them common in kids' rooms. Anything dense, like tools or stacks of paper, can pull a fabric bin out of shape, so use rail drawers for those.

finalTake: The FINETONES double-wide is the right bookshelf with drawers for most rooms with a free 40 inches of wall, since four drawers and eight shelves store everything. The DICTAC fits narrow walls, and the Furologee is the budget corner pick. Check depth and anti-tip hardware before style.
